note: The Java packages each loader in eras/minecraft.json puts in a mod's reach (and each plugin platform in a plugin's), and the game's own. The pure layer may mention none of them (docs/eras.md, law P1); myceliumPurity reads this file, so a loader named in an era is guarded as soon as it is named here, and the repository check fails if an era names a loader this file does not. Each entry says where its packages come from, so it can be re-verified: a loader's packages are what its own published artifacts declare, not what its name suggests. 'family' says what kind of artifact the loader runs: 'mod' (reaches into the game), 'plugin' (reaches the game only through a published API) or 'agent' (a Java agent); a wall that names a family splits every loader of it. 'compat' says where a built artifact declares the Minecraft versions it accepts, so the range gate can read what the loader will enforce: the file in the artifact's resources (the first that exists), its format ('json': 'path' is dotted keys with [key=value] selecting an array element; 'toml': a table, its 'where' keys and the 'key' wanted; 'yaml': a top-level 'key'), and the 'syntax' its value is written in ('semver': Fabric and Quilt, 'maven': Forge and NeoForge, 'api-version': Bukkit); 'compatFrom' borrows another loader's. 'from' and 'before' say, where the file began later than the loader did, where an older artifact declares it instead. A loader with no 'compat' enforces none the build can read.

game.source: Minecraft itself, and Mojang's own libraries it ships with (Brigadier, DataFixerUpper, authlib)

tools.source: Mixin (org.spongepowered:mixin): bytecode injection into the game, platform by definition

javaagent.source: Java Instrumentation API in the Java 8 platform, used as an exact-profile native entrance rather than a Minecraft mod loader

fabric.source: Fabric Loader and Fabric API (net.fabricmc:fabric-loader, net.fabricmc.fabric-api:fabric-api on maven.fabricmc.net)

forge.source: Forge (net.minecraftforge:forge on maven.minecraftforge.net); cpw.mods is FML before 1.13 and ModLauncher/SecureJarHandler after

compat.before: Forge reads the Minecraft versions a mod accepts from its @Mod annotation (acceptedMinecraftVersions) before 1.13, which is code the build does not read

neoforge.source: NeoForge (net.neoforged:neoforge on maven.neoforged.net); cpw.mods is the ModLauncher its early versions ran on

quilt.source: Quilt Loader and QSL (org.quiltmc:quilt-loader, org.quiltmc.qsl on maven.quiltmc.org); Quilted Fabric API keeps Fabric API's net.fabricmc packages

legacy-fabric.source: Fabric Loader with Legacy Fabric API (net.legacyfabric.legacy-fabric-api on repo.legacyfabric.net)

ornithe.source: Fabric Loader with Ornithe's Standard Libraries (net.ornithemc:osl on maven.ornithemc.net)

babric.source: Fabric Loader on Beta 1.7.3 (github.com/babric) with StationAPI (net.modificationstation.stationapi, github.com/ModificationStation/StationAPI)

bukkit.source: The Bukkit API as Spigot publishes it (org.spigotmc:spigot-api on hub.spigotmc.org, from 1.8), with its BungeeCord chat components (net.md_5.bungee.api.chat); CraftBukkit and every fork implement it

spigot.source: Spigot (org.spigotmc:spigot-api on hub.spigotmc.org; BuildTools builds the server from 1.8): the Bukkit API plus org.spigotmc

paper.source: Paper's API (io.papermc.paper:paper-api on repo.papermc.io): the Bukkit API plus io.papermc/com.destroystokyo.paper, and the Adventure text library (net.kyori) it ships; builds from 1.7.10 (fill.papermc.io)

purpur.source: Purpur's API (org.purpurmc.purpur:purpur-api on repo.purpurmc.org): Paper's API plus org.purpurmc.purpur (net.pl3x.purpur in its early builds); builds from 1.14.1 (api.purpurmc.org)

folia.source: Folia's API (dev.folia:folia-api on repo.papermc.io): Paper's API with the threaded regions in io.papermc.paper.threadedregions; builds from 1.19.4 (fill.papermc.io); a plugin declares folia-supported: true in plugin.yml
